hyperedges.label: Detect -> AST + Semantic -> Merge Extraction Flow

nodes.label: Step B0 Semantic Cache Check
nodes.rationale: Always (re)writes the cache file, or deletes any leftover from a prior run, so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json (#1392).

nodes.label: Step B1 Chunk Splitting
nodes.rationale: Chunks of 20-25 files grouped by directory so related artifacts land in the same chunk and cross-file relationships are more likely extracted; each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context.

nodes.label: Step B2 Parallel Subagent Dispatch
nodes.rationale: All subagents are dispatched in a single response so they run in parallel rather than serially.

nodes.label: Discrete Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; the production bimodal distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) shows range guidance collapsing to a binary, so a fixed value set replaces it and low-confidence edges must be marked AMBIGUOUS instead of scored below 0.4.

nodes.label: Step B3 Cache and Merge Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunk file existence on disk is the success signal; missing or invalid chunks are warned about and skipped rather than silently dropped or aborting the run. Real token counts are read from the subagent usage field because the chunk JSON always carries placeholder zeros.

nodes.label: Part C AST + Semantic Merge
nodes.rationale: AST nodes go first and semantic nodes are deduplicated by id so structural extraction wins on collisions.

nodes.label: Empty Graph Guard
nodes.rationale: Checked immediately after build and before any write, because an empty extraction must not clobber a good graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, or analysis sidecar (#1392).

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to overwrite an existing graph.json with fewer nodes (#479); the report is only written if the graph actually persisted, because a report describing a graph that was not written would be a lie (#1392).

nodes.label: Step 5 Community Labeling
nodes.rationale: graph.json is re-exported after labeling so nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490); questions are regenerated because labels affect question phrasing.

nodes.label: --directed Graph Mode
nodes.rationale: IS_DIRECTED is substituted everywhere: True builds a DiGraph preserving source->target direction, False builds the default undirected Graph.

nodes.label: Step 6 Obsidian Vault Export
nodes.rationale: Opt-in behind --obsidian because it generates one file per node.

nodes.label: Step 6 HTML Graph Export
nodes.rationale: Generated by default so the output opens in any browser with no server needed.

nodes.label: Aggregated Community View Above 5000 Nodes
nodes.rationale: Graphs above the 5000-node limit are collapsed to a community meta-graph with cross-community edge counts; a single-community graph skips HTML because the aggregated view is not useful.

nodes.label: Step 6b Agent-Crawlable Wiki
nodes.rationale: Recommended fallback for graphs too large to render as HTML and the most useful output for an autonomous agent navigating the graph between sessions; run before cleanup so .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: Step 7 Neo4j Export and Push
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so the push is safe to re-run without creating duplicates.

nodes.label: Step 7b SVG Export
nodes.rationale: SVG embeds in Obsidian, Notion, and GitHub READMEs.

nodes.label: Step 7c GraphML Export
nodes.rationale: Opens in Gephi, yEd, or any GraphML tool.

nodes.label: Step 7d MCP stdio Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live.

nodes.label: Step 8 Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Skipped silently below 5000 words because for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Step 9 Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that produced output are stamped, so a failed chunk is re-queued next run instead of being lost (#2015).

nodes.label: Post-Pipeline Guided Exploration
nodes.rationale: Only God Nodes, Surprising Connections, and Suggested Questions are pasted, then the single most boundary-crossing question is offered, so the session feels like navigation rather than a one-shot report — the graph is the map and the agent is the guide.

nodes.label: --update Incremental Re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new or changed files to save tokens and time; deletions alone still produce an empty extraction so the merge step can prune.

nodes.label: Code-Only Change Shortcut
nodes.rationale: If every changed file has a code extension, semantic extraction is skipped entirely because AST extraction needs no LLM.

nodes.label: Graph Diff After Update
nodes.rationale: The old graph.json is copied to .graphify_old.json before merging so a before/after diff can be shown.

nodes.label: --cluster-only Re-clustering
nodes.rationale: Re-exports graph.json without community_labels because labels are still placeholders at this point; Step 5 re-exports with curated names (#2490).

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands
nodes.rationale: Re-resolves the Python interpreter if .graphify_python is missing, e.g. after the user deleted graphify-out/; the shebang is rejected if it contains unexpected characters.

nodes.label: /graphify query
nodes.rationale: Answers using only what the graph contains and quotes source_location when citing a fact, rather than hallucinating edges.

nodes.label: BFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode, explores neighbors layer by layer to depth 3 — best for 'what is X connected to?' broad-context questions.

nodes.label: DFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Follows one path as deep as possible with a depth limit of 6 to avoid traversing the whole graph — best for tracing a specific chain or dependency path.

nodes.label: Token-Budget Aware Query Output
nodes.rationale: Nodes are ranked by term-overlap relevance and the output is truncated at roughly 4 chars per token so the answer fits the budget.

nodes.label: save-result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Query, path, and explain answers are written back into the graph so they improve future queries.

nodes.label: /graphify add URL Ingestion
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects Twitter/X (oEmbed), arXiv, PDF, image, and generic webpage URLs; after a successful save the --update pipeline runs automatically on ./raw.

nodes.label: --watch Background Watcher
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; docs/papers/images only set a needs_update flag. Debounce waits until file activity stops so a wave of parallel agent writes doesn't trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: post-commit Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process, so it works with any editor; doc and image changes are ignored and need a manual --update.

nodes.label: graphify devin install
nodes.rationale: Writes a graphify section to .windsurf/rules/graphify.md so Devin checks the graph before answering codebase questions and rebuilds after code changes.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS when unsure), never skip the corpus check warning, always show token cost, and never hide cohesion scores behind symbols.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (droid variant)
nodes.rationale: Framed so any codebase question is treated as a graphify query first when graphify-out/ exists.

nodes.label: --help Short-Circuit
nodes.rationale: On --help/-h the Usage block is printed verbatim and nothing else runs — no detect, no default path, no commands.

nodes.label: Fast Path for Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, Steps 1-5 are skipped and the query runs immediately — the graph is already built, so re-detecting or asking the user to narrow wastes time.

nodes.label: Step 0 GitHub Clone and Multi-Path Merge
Step 1 Interpreter Detection and Install
nodes.rationale: Resolves uv tool, pipx shebang, then python3 in order because that ordering is most reliable on modern Mac/Linux; the resolved path is persisted to .graphify_python so every later step uses the same interpreter.

nodes.label: Step 2 File Detection
nodes.rationale: The detect sidecar is written from Python rather than a shell redirect so the same block renders on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).

nodes.label: Skipped Sensitive Files Report
nodes.rationale: Skipped file names are listed so a wrongly-flagged source or doc is visible and can be renamed or moved (#2106).

nodes.label: Corpus Size Warning and Narrowing
nodes.rationale: Above 2M words or 500 files the top-5 subdirectories are offered for narrowing; graphify-out sidecars are filtered out of the ranking, and if every file is at root there are no subfolders to narrow to, so --no-cluster is suggested instead.

nodes.label: Step 2.5 Video and Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are treated as doc files in Step 3.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Policy
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally via AST with no LLM, so a code-only corpus needs nothing; only docs/papers/images need semantic extraction, and that falls to the host agent itself when no Gemini key is set. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are never read, so prompting for one is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Extraction Backend
nodes.rationale: Used only when GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, via extract_corpus_parallel instead of subagent dispatch; default model gemini-3-flash-preview, overridable with GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: Parallel AST + Semantic Dispatch
nodes.rationale: AST and semantic passes operate on different file types and can run simultaneously; parallelizing saves 5-15s on large corpora since AST is deterministic and fast.

nodes.label: Part B Code-Only Fast Path
nodes.rationale: An empty .graphify_semantic.json must still be written because Part C reads it unconditionally; without it a code-only run hits FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Mandatory Agent Tool Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Reading files one-by-one instead of dispatching subagents is 5-10x slower, so the Agent/Task tool is required.

nodes.label: Extraction Spec as Cache Attribution Key
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to references/extraction-spec.md because it is the extraction prompt: when an upgrade changes the prompt, old entries are re-extracted rather than replayed, and unchanged prompts keep their entries (#1939).

nodes.label: Content-Files-Only Semantic Scope
nodes.rationale: Only document, paper, and image categories go to semantic extraction; code is already covered by the AST pass, and flattening every category makes subagents re-read every source file (#1392).

nodes.label: --mode deep
nodes.rationale: DEEP_MODE must be passed to every subagent and tracked from the original invocation so it is not lost mid-pipeline; it produces richer INFERRED edges.

nodes.label: Absolute Chunk Path Requirement
nodes.rationale: CHUNK_PATH is derived from the current working directory, where Part C globs graphify-out/ — not from .graphify_root or the scan directory (#1392).
